newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission counts on rice talks to end rice row.
newsitem.headline: Commission counts on rice talks to end rice row.

text.p: The European Union is relying on talks with United States officials to resolve a growing dispute over its failure to adopt GATT minimum quotas for U.S. rice, a Commission official said on Monday.
"There is such united opposition to the proposal from member states that there is little point in returning to the matter in the weekly cereals and rice management committee," the official said.
Commission insiders say unless the U.S. can be persuaded to change its position the matter seems certain to be dealt with by a World Trade Organisation (WTO) complaints panel in Geneva.

"We are holding talks with U.S. officials and that is all we can do. We have to review our position but at the moment there are no plans to take the issue back to the management committee," the official said.
Trade organisations oppose article 24/6 of the GATT agreement on increased maximum quotas to allow for enlargement.

Under the deal the U.S. is granted an extra tariff-free quota for 38,000 tonnes of milled rice and 8,000 tonnes of brown rice. A Commission proposal which would implement the GATT deal on additional quota is opposed by European rice producer countries who see their existing protection being eroded.
They are supported by mainly northern rice milling countries which fear increased white rice imports, a Commission official explained.
A U.S. spokesman in Brussels said that the EU will be in default of the agreement on January 1, 1997, adding "the ball is entirely in the Commission's court."
